### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **72** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**46** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cf450262d376e053bc3a0975fcccea822605dc08` — the merge of head `c3c3890761533334ae630ffcb420bfac1af7acb9` into base `0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cf450262d376e053bc3a0975fcccea822605dc08 && git checkout cf450262d376e053bc3a0975fcccea822605dc08
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a c3c3890761533334ae630ffcb420bfac1af7acb9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a && git merge --no-ff c3c3890761533334ae630ffcb420bfac1af7acb9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `263b1dc51ee8261c823dbc7363ba2a8836ad3955`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/DraftConflictDialog.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/studioSaveBar.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx. The rest of the diff (tests, the changeset prose, the generated `protocol.mdx` and `authorable-surface/api.json`, the i18n catalogues) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs read: card #36601 body and its four comments (triage 7089618771, claim 7096852442, progress 7103696854, dev report 7103778017), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `origin/main`, and the check-runs on this head. Check-runs when read: 1 failure (`Check Changeset`), 21 success, 9 skipped, 35 still in progress (all `Test Core` and `Test UI` shards, `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint UI`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`). No in-progress run is cited as green below.

### ① Derived judgments

- `PublishMetaItemRequestSchema.parentVersion` (`string | null`, optional): RIGHT as a widening of the request. Absent stays unpinned: the REST door spreads the key only when a header was sent (`meta-item-history-routes.ts`), `promoteDraftForPublish` reads the active head only when the key is present, and `repo.promoteDraft` falls back to `currentActive?.hash ?? null` exactly as on `main`. The batch `publishPackageDrafts` path builds its own request and states no pin, as the jsdoc says.
- `GetMetaItemLayeredResponseSchema.overlayVersion` (`string | null`, optional): RIGHT as a widening of the answer. Served only under `opts.withVersion`, which the two doors (`rest-server.ts`, `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`) turn on; in-process readers get no key, which the description's "absent means not served" covers.
- The pinned compare is at the address the promotion writes: `repo.headAt(ref, { state: 'active', packageId: promoteInto })` in the protocol and `put(..., packageId: activePackageId)` in the repository resolve the same row in every branch I traced (stated package; unbound draft adopted into the item's package; row-held base). RIGHT.
- The single-item publish has ONE door. `publishMetaItem` is called only from `packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts`; the runtime `/meta` domain serves `/layers` but no per-item publish, so there is no second door that serves the token and ignores the pin. RIGHT.
- Stale token → `InboundVersionConflictError` thrown inside the promotion's `try`, answered through `metadataConflictRefusal` as 409 `METADATA_CONFLICT` with `currentVersion` (keyed, or `null`); an empty or raw token is never read as "no pin" (`storedParentForToken`). Nothing is written before the refusal. RIGHT.
- Is anything narrowed? One thing, and the PR's sentence does not name it: on `main` the publish door read neither `If-Match` nor `If-None-Match`, so a publish carrying either succeeded; on this head a stale `If-Match` is 409, and `If-None-Match` with a value other than `*`, or beside `If-Match`, is 400. The 409 is the card's ask 2 verbatim. I found no first-party sender on `main`: `@objectstack/client` `publishItem` and `MetadataClient.publish` send neither header. I judge the `(widening)` arm to hold (a caller that sent a precondition asked for the guard; no declared capability is taken away), with the wording nit N1.
- No Studio Save that succeeded before is refused for a single editor: load pins `overlayVersion`, each landed publish re-pins from the receipt's `version` (the same `receiptVersion` producer), and a server that serves no `overlayVersion` leaves the publish unpinned.

### ② Semver level

WRONG on this head, by the gate's own verdict. `Check Changeset` concluded `failure` on `263b1dc5`: the diff moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` (two keys added: `api/GetMetaItemLayeredResponse:overlayVersion`, `api/PublishMetaItemRequest:parentVersion`) while the PR body and the changeset declare `Metadata-protocol: none` and grade `@objectstack/spec` `patch`. The gate reads a changed authorable-surface shard as a metadata-protocol change and requires `Metadata-protocol: added` with at least `minor` on the package that carries it.

M1 (must-fix) — declare `Metadata-protocol: added` in the PR body and in `.changeset/36601-published-layer-version-pin.md`, and grade `@objectstack/spec` at least `minor`. The baseline shard is correct as generated and must not be edited to quiet the gate.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: the arm holds (see ①). No removal, no tombstone, no ADR-0087 disposition owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (the object extension, hooks, pair-actions and flow editors still publish unpinned): answered, option A. The server half covers every editor, an unpinned publish is today's behaviour (card ruling 3), and the card's re-check is the object page. Condition: the follow-up card is filed before this PR closes #36601, because those four editors keep the silent overwrite the card describes.
- Dev flag, `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` NOT-MEASURED and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` declared to CI: the runs that would answer them (`Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Build Core`) were still in progress when read. Not answered green by this record.
- Dev flag, file surface: the diff stays inside the claimed surface (metadata-protocol, rest, runtime meta domain, spec, the Studio conflict wiring under `ui/`). No breach.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds one keyed head read per pinned publish (`repo.headAt`) and one `readVersionToken` per door `/layers` read (an address resolution plus a keyed head read). No id materialisation, no in-app join. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, against card #36601 asks 1 to 3 and its first consumer (Studio's object page): the two members implement the asks. The card's race is closed for the wired editor: B's publish is compared, at the promoting write's address, against the token of the row B loaded; after A's publish that token is stale and B is refused before anything is promoted. I tried the overwrite path (re-pinned to the refusal's `currentVersion`, a third publish in between is asked about again), the first-publish path (`null` → `If-None-Match: *`, refused once a row exists), a guessed raw hash (refused), and a legacy row with no stored checksum (served version accepted by `lockAccepts`). None broke.

S1 (should-fix) — `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`: `overlay` and `overlayVersion` come from two separate reads with no transaction around them, and the token is read LAST (the `findServedOverlayRow` read near line 533, the `readVersionToken` read near line 957, many awaits apart). A publish that lands between them is served as the OLD body with the NEW token; Studio then pins a stale buffer to the current version and its Save replaces the other editor's change without a dialog. That is the card's lost update inside one request's duration, and the seat ruling on #36511 rejected a fix that "narrows the window but cannot close it". Fix: take the token from the same row read that serves the layer when that row is the address's row, or read the token BEFORE the body so a tear can only produce a false 409, never a false accept.

S2 (should-fix) — `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/studioSaveBar.tsx` with `DraftConflictDialog.tsx` (`DraftVersionGuard.publish`, reload branch): `discardSavedDraft` swallows a failed `reset`, and the guard then clears both pins and reloads anyway. The reload installs the losing draft (the author's stale-based body) as the buffer and pins it to the FRESH published version, so the next Save publishes over the other editor's change with no second prompt. The comment "the re-read installs the live row, never the draft that lost" holds only when the discard succeeds. Fix: when the discard fails, do not re-pin to the fresh row (keep the stale published pin, or surface the failure instead of reloading).

N1 (nit) — the `Clause-②` sentence says "nothing is removed or narrowed". Precise form: publish requests that carried `If-Match` or `If-None-Match` were ignored on `main` and are now honoured (409) or refused when malformed (400). Prose only; accepted deviation if left.

N2 (nit) — `sys-metadata-repository.ts`, `expectedActiveHash` jsdoc: "the check and the write are one call, not a read and a later write" overstates. `put` reads the head, compares, then updates by row id inside `engine.transaction`; the update carries no condition on the checksum, and `withTxn`'s own docblock declares the degrade on drivers without rollback or isolation. It is the same lock the save door has always used (the card's named precedent), so two publishes overlapping at transaction scale are as protected as two saves are, no more. The card's race (a stale read, human scale) is closed regardless. Accepted deviation; a conditional write is a follow-up for ADR-0008, not this card.

N3 (nit) — `protocol.zod.ts`, `overlayVersion` description: the token is the row at the read's SAVE address, which is not always the row `overlay` shows (ADR-0048 fallback, an ADR-0146 served override) and, for a read naming no package, not always the row an unnamed publish replaces (a bundle member whose rows a base and a declaring package both hold; an action's environment-own draft; an unbound item whose only draft is package-bound). In those cases the pinned publish answers a false 409, never a false accept, because the pin is judged at the promotion's own address. "The published layer a publish of this item replaces" should say so. Studio's object page names the package on both calls and is not affected. Follow-up or prose fix.

N4 (nit) — `DraftConflictDialog.tsx`, `DraftVersionGuard.publish`: every 409 `METADATA_CONFLICT` on the publish is shown as a published-layer conflict, including the pre-existing "draft changed after this publish judged it" refusal, whose `currentVersion` is the DRAFT's token. Overwrite then re-pins the publish to a draft token, is refused once more, and lands on the second confirmation. Safe direction, clumsy; follow-up.

N5 (nit) — `meta-item-history-routes.ts`: the 400 sentences reused from `metaSaveRequestOptions` say "saves only over that version" on the publish door. Wording only.

`protocol.ts`, `rest-server.ts`, `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`, `metadata-client.ts`, `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`: agree with the contract as written; the facade's return type now reuses the facet's, with no member lost.

## 维护者速读

- 结论：退回修改（REWORK）。整体设计成立：Studio 对象页两人同时保存时，后保存的人会看到冲突提示，不再悄悄覆盖。
- 但有两处小漏洞会让覆盖仍然悄悄发生：读取已发布内容和读取版本号是两次分开的读；以及“重新加载”时撤回草稿失败会被吞掉。两处都需要改代码，改完由本审核线程复核。
- 其余编辑器（流程、钩子等）仍未加保护，需要另开后续卡。无需你做任何事。

## 席位核对

Verdict: **REWORK** · head `612759dfd823e6759a08541ae4b4d19010315b8f` · card #36601 · L2 record: comment 7103982658 at `263b1dc51ee8261c823dbc7363ba2a8836ad3955` (FAIL: M1, S1, S2)

Reviewed against GitHub (diff, card body, `l1-face.mjs`, `pr-state.mjs`), not against the report. Between `263b1dc5` and `612759df` only `.changeset/36601-published-layer-version-pin.md` moves (spec `minor`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, the authorable-surface sentence), so the L2 record's reading of every code path stands at this head.

### Checklist
- Shape: open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36601`. `Fixes` is acceptable on the card's own Re-check (one object, two sessions): the server side is complete and the object page is wired. The four other Studio editors that still publish unpinned (object extension, hooks, pair actions, flow) are declared in the body's "Not in this PR" and owe a follow-up card filed before this PR closes #36601 (the L2 answered the dev's open question the same way).
- Changeset and `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` sentences read against the diff: both new members, the `If-Match` / `If-None-Match: *` reading, `409 METADATA_CONFLICT` with `currentVersion`, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` for both headers or a non-`*` `If-None-Match`, unpinned when neither header, the client options and the four locale keys hold. The L2's N1 (requests carrying those headers were ignored on main and can now be refused) is accepted under the `(widening)` arm: no first-party sender sent them on main.
- UI read by this seat (TIER_DEFAULT): `DraftVersionGuard.publish` takes `beforeReload` before `reload` and clears both pins; "keep editing" throws a marked error that the page shows as the draft conflict's "not saved"; `publishSavedItem` keeps its unpinned overload byte-compatible for the six other callers.
- M1 (L2, `Check Changeset` red at `263b1dc5`): closed by `612759df`; re-read on the fixed head.
- Gates at `612759df`: 11 success, 0 failed, 29 pending when read; re-read on the fixed head.

### REWORK items
1. **S1, confirmed in the tree:** `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` reads the overlay body first and `overlayVersion` afterwards (`readVersionToken(…, 'active')`), as two reads with no transaction. A publish that lands between them serves the OLD body with the NEW token, so Studio installs a stale buffer pinned to the current version, and its next Save overwrites the other editor without a prompt. This is the exact lost update the card closes. Fix: take the token from the same row read as the overlay, or read the token BEFORE the body (a stale token then gives a false `409`, the safe direction). Add a pin that interleaves a publish between the two reads.
2. **S2, confirmed in the tree:** on a published conflict answered "reload", `publishSavedItem`'s `discardSavedDraft` swallows a failed `reset`, and the guard reloads anyway. The reload installs the losing draft (`draft ?? overlay ?? code`), and `recordPublished` pins it to the fresh published version, so the next Save overwrites with no prompt. Fix: when the discard fails, do not reload into the draft (surface the failure and keep the conflict open, or reload without installing that draft). Add a pin with a `reset` that rejects.
3. Nits N2–N5 from the L2 are accepted deviations; N3 and N4 are better addressed in the follow-up card above.

The L2 delta on the fixed head is read by the same reviewer.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ee46e5e2c9c6a1b3e4e71c7288f35fbc85c33b1d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/DraftConflictDialog.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/studioSaveBar.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx. The rest of the diff is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Delta review of the record on head `263b1dc5` (comment 7103982658). Read: the changeset-only move `263b1dc5` to `612759df`, the five-file delta `612759df` to `ee46e5e2` (`protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`, `DraftConflictDialog.tsx`, `studioSaveBar.tsx`, two test files), the PR body, follow-up card #36726, and the check-runs on `ee46e5e2`. Check-runs when read: 10 success (`Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`, `filter`), 9 skipped, 18 in progress (`Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, every `Lint` job, the four `Type Check` jobs, the two shard planners, `Live E2E UI`); the test shards had not been created yet. No in-progress run is cited as green, and the two new tests are not confirmed by CI in this record.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept-set or public-surface change in the delta. `protocol.zod.ts` and the two schema members are untouched since `263b1dc5`; the judgments of the first record stand. The reorder in `getMetaItemLayered` changes which read runs first, not what is served: the same producer (`readVersionToken`, `active`, the read's address and member), the same `null` and absent cases.

### ② Semver level

M1: closed. The changeset on this head grades `@objectstack/spec` `minor` and declares `Metadata-protocol: added`; the PR body carries the same line; `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on `ee46e5e2`. The other six packages stay `patch`, which the rule allows (the kind is carried by spec). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is unchanged and holds as judged before. The new `Skills-docs: none` line is right: the two members are wire members a client sends and reads, nothing a metadata author writes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (four editors still publish unpinned): the condition of the first record is met. #36726 is filed, open, marked blocked by #36601, and names the four call sites and what each needs.
- Author's residual, the `hadDraft` case: answered below as N6; it does not reopen S2.
- SQL push-down: the delta moves one existing keyed read earlier and adds none. No finding.
- The dev's two gates declared to CI (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) sit in runs still in progress on this head. Not answered green here.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed. `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` now reads `overlayVersion` before the overlay body (ahead of the `findServedOverlayRow` read, and so ahead of `effective` and the draft layer). A publish landing between the two reads can only pair an old token with a newer body, and the Save's pinned publish is then refused 409: the safe direction. `member` is resolved above the new position, and the failed-read rule (`rethrowUnlessMetadataStoreUnprovisioned`) moved with the block unchanged.

S2: closed. `publishSavedItem` hands the guard `discardBeforeReload`, which does not swallow a failed `reset`. The throw leaves `DraftVersionGuard.publish` before the pins are cleared and before `deps.reload()`, so the stale published pin stays and nothing is re-read. `publishSavedItem`'s `catch` then answers a refused Save; the metadata pulse it emits cannot install the losing draft, because the object page holds its buffers while `dirty` or `saving` is set (`objBuffersHeld`), and a refused Save leaves the page dirty. The next Save is asked again.

N6 (nit) — the `hadDraft` residual. When a draft was already pending before the Save, a reload keeps it by design (it may be a copilot's), so the re-read installs that draft, now carrying the page's edits, pinned to the fresh published version. I judge this acceptable as a follow-up and not S2 again, for three reasons. First, the draft pin stops the two-Studio-Saves race before the publish pin is reached: both editors share the pending draft, and the second draft save is refused. Reaching the residual needs a writer that moves the active row without touching the draft (a direct active save, a rollback) while a draft is pending. Second, the author is asked once, and what the page shows after the reload is the pending draft, which is what it showed before the Save. Third, a pending draft built on an older published row is the draft model's standing condition on `main` (publishing it from Changes has the same effect), and discarding a draft the Save did not create is not this card's to decide. Condition on the follow-up: #36726 as read covers the four unpinned editors only and does not mention this case; add it there, or file it on its own, before #36601 closes.

N1 to N5 of the first record: unchanged, none fixed in this delta, none moved by it. They stay nits: accepted deviations or follow-ups.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
